content: 1. Ephedrine is indicated for the treatment of clinically significant hypotension occurring during anesthesia. However, its safety and efficacy have not been fully established. It is recommended to start at the lower end of the dosing range, especially in patients with reduced hepatic, renal, or cardiac function, or those with concurrent diseases or on other drug therapies. Since ephedrine is primarily excreted by the kidneys, patients with impaired renal function may have an increased risk of adverse reactions. Elderly patients, who are more likely to have reduced renal function, should have their dose carefully selected, and renal function should be monitored. 2. Ephedrine decreases the effects of iobenguane I-123 by receptor binding competition. This interaction is contraindicated. If clinically appropriate, discontinue drugs that compete for norepinephrine receptor sites for at least five half-lives prior to imaging, as they may cause false-negative imaging results. 3. Isocarboxazid increases the effects of ephedrine through pharmacodynamic synergism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of acute hypertensive episodes. 4. Linezolid increases the effects of ephedrine through pharmacodynamic synergism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of acute hypertensive episodes. 5. Phenelzine increases the effects of ephedrine through pharmacodynamic synergism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of acute hypertensive episodes. 6. Procarbazine increases the effects of ephedrine through pharmacodynamic synergism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of acute hypertensive episodes. 7. Rasagiline increases the effects of ephedrine through pharmacodynamic synergism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of acute hypertensive episodes. 8. Selegiline increases the effects of ephedrine through pharmacodynamic synergism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of acute hypertensive episodes. 9. Selegiline transdermal increases the effects of ephedrine through pharmacodynamic synergism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of acute hypertensive episodes. 10. Tranylcypromine increases the effects of ephedrine through pharmacodynamic synergism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of acute hypertensive episodes. 11. Tricyclic antidepressants (e.g., amitriptyline, amoxapine, clomipramine, desipramine, doxepin, imipramine, nortriptyline, protriptyline, trimipramine) may increase or decrease the effects of ephedrine. This occurs by blocking norepinephrine reuptake or blocking the uptake of indirect sympathomimetics into adrenergic neurons. It is recommended to avoid or use alternative drugs and monitor closely. 12. Cabergoline increases the effects of ephedrine through pharmacodynamic synergism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of additive vasospasm and hypertension. 13. Desflurane increases the toxicity of ephedrine through an unknown mechanism. It is recommended to avoid or use an alternative drug due to the risk of ventricular tachycardia and hypertension. 14. Dihydroergotamine (including intranasal formulations) increases the effects of ephedrine through pharmacodynamic synergism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of additive vasospasm and hypertension. 15. Doxapram increases the effects of ephedrine through pharmacodynamic synergism. It is recommended to avoid or use an alternative drug due to the risk of additive pressor effects. 16. Ergotamine increases the effects of ephedrine through pharmacodynamic synergism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of additive vasospasm and hypertension. 17. Isoflurane increases the toxicity of ephedrine through an unknown mechanism. It is recommended to avoid or use an alternative drug due to the risk of ventricular tachycardia and hypertension. 18. Ketamine and ephedrine both increase each other's effects through pharmacodynamic synergism. This combination is contraindicated in situations where increased blood pressure would be hazardous, such as in hypertension, stroke, head trauma, or intracranial bleeding. 19. Methylergonovine increases the effects of ephedrine through pharmacodynamic synergism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of additive vasospasm and hypertension. 20. Ozanimod increases the toxicity of ephedrine through sympathetic (adrenergic) effects, including increased blood pressure and heart rate. Co-administration is not recommended due to the potential for serious adverse reactions, including hypertensive crisis. Monitor for hypertension if used concomitantly. 21. Sympathomimetic drugs (e.g., amphetamine, albuterol, arformoterol, benzphetamine) and ephedrine both increase sympathetic (adrenergic) effects, including increased blood pressure and heart rate. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Beta-blockers (e.g., atenolol, bisoprolol, carvedilol) decrease the effects of ephedrine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Drugs that alter serum potassium levels (e.g., albuterol, amiloride, aspirin, bumetanide) may interact with ephedrine. The effect of these interactions is not clear, so caution and monitoring are advised. 24. Drugs that affect sedation (e.g., alprazolam, amobarbital, azelastine, butorphanol) may interact with ephedrine. The effect of these interactions is not clear, so caution and monitoring are advised.
